title: Grilled Shrimp Louie
description: Chef John substitutes smoky grilled shrimp for the traditional crab in this summery salad. Make the dressing ahead of time to let it chill, because the shrimp take just minutes to cook.
ingredients: 0.25 teaspoon kosher salt, or to taste
2 pounds uncooked medium shrimp - peeled and deveined, tails left intact
1 avocado - peeled, pitted, and thinly sliced

steps.text: Place mayonnaise, ketchup, creme fraiche, 1 tablespoon lemon juice, cider vinegar, brown sugar, paprika, salt, cayenne pepper, Worcestershire sauce, green onion, and parsley in a bowl. Whisk together until ingredients are well combined. Cover and refrigerate until thoroughly chilled, 2 to 3 hours.
Drizzle olive oil and juice from half a lemon over the shrimp just before grilling. Sprinkle with salt and smoked paprika. Gently but thoroughly toss until shrimp are coated.
Preheat an outdoor grill for high heat and lightly oil the grate.

Grill over hot coals until shrimp are pink and flesh is opaque, about 2 minutes per side. Transfer to a dish and refrigerate until shrimp are chilled, about 30 minutes. You can remove shrimp tails or leave them on.

Divide romaine lettuce among serving bowls. Arrange cherry tomatoes, avocado slices, and egg halves on top. Season with salt and pepper. Ladle on about 1/4 cup to 1/2 cup dressing on the vegetables, and top with the shrimp and sliced green onions. Drizzle additional dressing over the shrimp, if desired.

video.description: Chef John's take on a classic Louie dressing is the star of this show. Adding ketchup and creme fraiche to a mayonnaise base is the secret. Follow this with lemon juice, apple cider vinegar, brown sugar, worchestershire, some minced onion and spices, then mix all together thoroughly. Give the ingredients time to meld together by refrigerating for at least a few hours, at which time you can salt to taste. Grilled shrimp, hard-boiled eggs and avocado are placed on salad then topped with the Louie dressing for a perfect summer dinner.
